==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Flurl&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Verify.Flurl: an HttpTest, and each call it recorded, are written as a readable request
        // and response rather than as their raw object graphs.
        // It initializes Verify.Http itself when that has not already run, so it is called after it.
        VerifyFlurl.Initialize();

        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/FlurlTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Flurl&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using Flurl.Http;
using Flurl.Http.Testing;

// Verify.Flurl: Snapshots a Flurl HttpTest and the calls it recorded, instead of asserting on them one by one.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.Flurl
// Note: Verify.Flurl depends on Verify.Http and calls VerifyHttp.Initialize() itself when it has
// not already run, so a later explicit call throws "Already Initialized".
// Note: All http scrubbing and settings come from Verify.Http; this package adds only the two
// converters.
// Note: The package targets net10.0 only.
public class FlurlTests
{
    // Everything sent while the HttpTest is in scope is captured. Verifying the test itself
    // writes every call, in order, with the response Flurl was told to return.
    [Fact]
    public async Task HttpTest()
    {
        using var httpTest = new HttpTest();

        httpTest.RespondWith("OK");

        await "http://api.mysite.com/".GetAsync();
        await "http://api.mysite.com/".PostAsync(new StringContent("the content"));

        await Verify(httpTest);
    }

    // A single recorded call can be verified on its own, which keeps a snapshot focused when
    // the code under test makes calls that are not interesting.
    [Fact]
    public async Task SingleCall()
    {
        using var httpTest = new HttpTest();

        httpTest.RespondWith("OK");

        await "http://api.mysite.com/".GetAsync();

        await Verify(httpTest.CallLog.Single());
    }
}
